title: Case study: TF activity in memory vs. naive T cells
text: differential_deviation_test() tests motif difference deviation scores two groups. two groups parametric = TRUE test Welch t-test; p-values adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. returned mean_difference column unsigned, direction change computed separately. Differences oriented naive minus memory, positive value indicates higher deviation score naive state.
code: compare_subsets <- function(object, naive, memory) {     grp_all <- colData(object)$cell_type     keep <- grp_all %in% c(naive, memory)     grp <- factor(as.character(grp_all[keep]), levels = c(naive, memory))      dev_sub <- deviations(object)[, keep, drop = FALSE]     z_sub <- deviationZScores(object)[, keep, drop = FALSE]     is_naive <- grp == naive      res <- differential_deviation_test(         deviations = dev_sub,         groups = grp,         alternative = "two.sided",         parametric = TRUE,         padjMethod = "BH"     )     res$diff <- rowMeans(dev_sub[, is_naive, drop = FALSE]) -         rowMeans(dev_sub[, !is_naive, drop = FALSE])     res$zdiff <- rowMeans(z_sub[, is_naive, drop = FALSE]) -         rowMeans(z_sub[, !is_naive, drop = FALSE])     res[order(res$p_value_adjusted), ] }  tc_res <- compare_subsets(immuneDeviations, "Tc-Naive", "Tc-Mem") th_res <- compare_subsets(immuneDeviations, "Th-Naive", "Th-Mem")  head(tc_res, 8) #>                  motifs      p_value p_value_adjusted mean_difference #> BATF3             BATF3 8.849438e-20     5.566296e-17      0.11777405 #> BATF::JUN     BATF::JUN 2.282248e-19     7.177671e-17      0.11601928 #> BATF               BATF 5.255967e-19     1.102001e-16      0.11884510 #> JUN(var.2)   JUN(var.2) 1.529002e-18     2.404355e-16      0.11285040 #> JUNB               JUNB 4.117214e-17     5.179456e-15      0.12884298 #> FOSL2             FOSL2 5.469143e-17     5.733484e-15      0.08754993 #> FOSL1::JUND FOSL1::JUND 6.586962e-17     5.918856e-15      0.10381391 #> TBR1               TBR1 1.071089e-16     8.421438e-15      0.07404221 #>                   diff    zdiff #> BATF3       0.11777405 2.033917 #> BATF::JUN   0.11601928 2.011964 #> BATF        0.11884510 2.027036 #> JUN(var.2)  0.11285040 2.036036 #> JUNB        0.12884298 1.913842 #> FOSL2       0.08754993 1.681151 #> FOSL1::JUND 0.10381391 1.684212 #> TBR1        0.07404221 1.889798

text: CD8 CD4 contrasts computed disjoint sets samples. Plotting Z-score differences shows whether two compartments identify motifs.  effect sizes correlated share sign motifs, factors recovered compartments.
code: shared <- intersect(tc_res$motifs, th_res$motifs) agree <- data.frame(     motifs = shared,     tc = tc_res$zdiff[match(shared, tc_res$motifs)],     th = th_res$zdiff[match(shared, th_res$motifs)] ) agree$sig_both <-     tc_res$p_value_adjusted[match(shared, tc_res$motifs)] < 0.05 &         th_res$p_value_adjusted[match(shared, th_res$motifs)] < 0.05  rho <- cor(agree$tc, agree$th) round(rho, 3) #> [1] 0.864 sum(agree$sig_both) #> [1] 268 # Label the extremes at both ends: the strongest motifs cluster tightly, # so ranking by magnitude alone places every label in one corner. ranked <- agree[order(agree$tc + agree$th), ] labelled <- rbind(head(ranked, 4), tail(ranked, 4))  ggplot(agree, aes(tc, th)) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +     geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +     geom_point(aes(colour = sig_both), size = 1.8, alpha = 0.85) +     geom_text(         data = labelled, aes(label = motifs),         size = 3, vjust = -0.8, check_overlap = TRUE     ) +     scale_colour_manual(         values = c("FALSE" = "grey75", "TRUE" = "#4292C6"),         name = "significant in both"     ) +     labs(         x = "CD8: Z-score difference (naive - memory)",         y = "CD4: Z-score difference (naive - memory)",         title = sprintf("Pearson r = %.2f", rho)     ) +     theme_classic() +     theme(         legend.position = "bottom",         axis.title.x = element_text(colour = cell_type_colors[["Tc-Mem"]]),         axis.title.y = element_text(colour = cell_type_colors[["Th-Mem"]])     )

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: DNA methylation can modulate transcription factor (TF) binding, particularly occurring within transcription factor binding sites (TFBS). methylTFR R package identifies DNA methylation signatures TFBS using whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) data. sample, methylation levels first aggregated across genomic regions corresponding TFBS. yields observed deviation, captures raw signal methylation enrichment depletion TF. account sequence composition biases, methylTFR estimates expected deviation using genomic background models derived TF motif GC content genome-wide GC frequency. deviation matrix provides compact interpretable representation TFBS methylation across samples, suitable downstream analyses dimensionality reduction (e.g., PCA, UMAP), clustering, differential testing, visualization TF-specific methylation footprints.

title: methylTFR: Quantification of DNA Methylation Signatures in Transcription Factor Binding Sites
text: methylTFR relies several precomputed annotation resources estimate expected methylation levels transcription factor binding sites (TFBS). annotations include: GC distribution (gcdist_subset): Genome-wide GC content distribution around cytosines, used model methylation expectations. Motif GC frequency (BATF_gcfreqs): GC frequency profile specific BATF motif across TFBS, used correct sequence composition bias.
